members.name: fibonacci_breakout_v1
members.thesis: After an initial intraday move (>0.5%), price often retraces to a Fibonacci level (38.2%, 50%, or 61.8%) before resuming in the original direction. The breakout occurs when price bounces off a Fib retracement level and breaks above the prior swing high (or below swing low for shorts), confirmed by v
entry_long: close pulled back to within 0.1% of fib_382 OR fib_500 OR fib_618
close > fib_level (bouncing off, not breaking through)
entry_short: close rallied to within 0.1% of (swing_low + 0.382 * range) OR (swing_low + 0.500 * range) OR (swing_low + 0.618 * range)
close < fib_level (rejecting at, not breaking through)
members.exit_target: fib_ext_1618 (161.8% Fibonacci extension of the original swing)
members.exit_stop: next Fibonacci level below entry (e.g., if entered at 38.2% bounce, stop at 61.8%)
filters: trade in direction of the initial swing (continuation bias)
weaknesses: Fibonacci levels have no fundamental mathematical basis in markets — they are purely self-fulfilling prophecy
Swing detection on 1-min bars is noisy; what constitutes a 'swing' is subjective despite the 5-bar pivot rule
The 161.8% extension target is ambitious and may not be reached intraday; more realistic target may be 100% (prior swing)
